translations.text: Many an island holds many kinds of living creatures far and wide. The Measurer, almighty God, raised up spacious lands for mankind, with equally many peoples and customs.
Never shall he [?] whose nest fails him; of necessity he shall be bound for a time.
A guiltless heart shall be glad. The blind man must do without his eyes; bright sight is denied him.
They cannot see the stars, the heaven-bright sun or the moon. That is painful to him in his mind, distressing when he alone knows it, and he does not expect that it will ever be reversed for him.

A sick man needs a physician. One must teach a young man, encourage and urge him so that he knows things well, until one has tamed him; one must give him food and clothing until one has brought him to understanding.
One must steer with a strong mind. The sea often brings storm, the ocean in grim seasons; the dark [waves] begin to rush fiercely from afar toward the land, to see whether it stands firm.
The walls hold out against them; the wind is shared by them both.

Just as the sea is calm when the wind does not rouse it, so peoples are at peace when they have come to terms. They settle in safe conditions, and then bold men hold their rightful kingdom with their companions.
God, who has many powers, shall alone unbind the fetters of frost. Winter shall depart, fair weather come again, summer hot with sun, and the sea restless.
A king shall buy a queen with goods, with cups and rings. Both must first be generous with gifts.
A ship shall be nailed, a shield bound, the light linden board. Dear is the welcome one to the Frisian wife when the vessel comes to rest;
his ship has come, and her husband is home, her own provider. She invites him in, washes his sea-stained clothing and gives him new garments, and on land she grants him what his love asks.
A woman shall keep faith with her man; often she is accused of wrongdoing. Many are steadfast, many are curious; they love strange men when the other goes far away.
The seafarer is long on his journey; yet one must always expect the beloved one, and wait for what one cannot hasten.
When the chance comes to him again, he comes home, if he lives unharmed, unless the sea hinders him and the ocean holds in its hands the joy of [?].

The man rich in goods then buys [?] a royal dwelling for the people, when he comes sailing; he makes use of wood and water when lodging is granted him, and buys food if he needs more, before he becomes too weary.
The lowly shall bow down, the sick sink down, the right [?]. Good counsel is most useful, evil most useless, which the wretched man takes.
Every mouth needs food; meals must come at their proper times.
Gold befits a man's sword, a splendid ornament of victory; treasure befits a queen; a good poet befits men, spear-strife befits warriors, to defend the peace of dwellings against war.
The shield is for the warrior, the spear-shaft for the robber; the ring is for the bride, books for the learner, the Eucharist for holy men, sins for the heathen.

Woden made idols; the Almighty made glory, the spacious heavens. That is the mighty God, the true King himself, Saviour of souls, who gave us everything by which we live, and who at the end will again rule over all mankind. That is the Measurer himself.
One shall speak counsel, write runes, sing songs, earn praise, pronounce judgement, and be busy every day.
One must treat a friend well on every road; often a man travels far around a town where he knows he has an uncertain friend.
Trees shall spread and faith grow, which rises up in the hearts of the innocent.
Deceit goes with wickedness, cunning with the [?]; thus the stone is stolen [?].
Cain struck down his own dear brother, whom that killing preserved [?]. Afterwards it was widely known that the endless hatred harmed mankind, as also the [?] peoples.
They suffered the strife of weapons widely across the earth, and devised and hardened the cruelly cutting sword.
